feature: A picked arrow's Appearance starts with its Arrow row
summary: Pick an arrow and Appearance now opens on Arrow, Chip, Color, Marker, Size and a closed Advanced, as the approved prototype draws it. Opacity, Blending and Masked by moved to the end of Advanced; a measurement works the same way, and every other layer still leads with Opacity.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/arrow-appearance-simple-walk.json (and measure-appearance-simple-walk.json).

try.do: Open a screenshot, press A and draw an arrow, type a caption and press Command Return.
try.shotNote: The window was behind another app when this was taken, so it shows the window's background look.

try.do: Read Appearance from the top: it starts at Arrow, with no Opacity above it.
Click Show beside Advanced and scroll to its end: Opacity, Blending and Masked by are there.
try.shotNote: The window was behind another app when this was taken, so it shows the window's background look.

try.do: Press I, click a gap to measure it, pick the measurement: Appearance starts at Chip.
try.shotNote: The window was behind another app when this was taken, so it shows the window's background look.

try.do: Draw a rectangle and pick it: Opacity still leads its Appearance.

evaluate: Does the arrow panel now read like the prototype from its first row?
Is the end of Advanced the right home for Opacity, Blending and Masked by on a mark, or would you rather find opacity somewhere you can reach without opening Advanced?
Is fading an arrow rare enough that one click on Show is a fair price?
rough: Row order now matches the prototype: Arrow, Chip, Color, Marker, Size, Advanced, and the shipped column starts at Arrow.

Opacity sits at the very end of an open Advanced, below Caption and its label rows, so on a short window it needs a scroll. Chose the end over the top of Advanced because the prototype's Advanced starts with Line and Head, and the shared rows are the least about the arrow itself.
